name: Invitations waiting for you (single-slot landing banner)
hostSurface: The surface a signed-in user actually lands on: web Place dashboard / hub StatusStrip; iOS Hub banner slot; Android HubSections banner region.
purpose: Make a waiting household invitation — and a dead one needing reissue — impossible to miss, without opening My Homes.
contents: One row: '{Inviter} invited you to {home}' + Review, backed by GET /api/homes/invitations (a dead client on web with zero callers, and no native client at all). Two or more reads 'You have 2 invitations' and opens the decision flow's index. The sender-side twin appears here too: '2 invitations need to be sent again'. Explicit precedence, one banner maximum: invite > reissue > setup > verify.
states: fetch failed (hide silently, never a broken banner)
entryPoints: Place dashboard / hub on every load
Push notification for a new invitation
visualization: A single-line banner with the inviter's name first and one action — the same slot shape the existing 'from the card in your mailbox' pill uses, so it reads as an arrival context rather than a new component. Never stacked with the setup or verify banners; the precedence rule is enforced in code, not by hope.
uxNote: The doc puts received invites only on My Homes, which a brand-new invitee — who usually has no home at all and lands on the Place dashboard — has no reason to open. Merging the doc's My Homes section into this banner removes a screen and fixes the entry-point bug at the same time. The sender half is what closes the INVITE_POLICY_CHANGED loop: without it the recipient is told to ask someone who can see nothing wrong.
